To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
early selection processing is involved in the Stroopeffect and the temporal modulation of attentional selection is a function of stimulus onset asynchrony (SOA).
early selection processing participates in the Stroops matching task phenomenon and that temporal modulation of early selection is a function of SOA.
the Stroop effect was maximal during simultaneous presentation of the two task stimuli, and was reduced at SOAs of 400 ms, and was inverted during SOA of 1,200.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the temporal dynamics of feature-based attentional selection.
the temporal dynamics of attentional processing in the Stropo task.
the temporal dynamics of feature-based attention in Stroop-like paradigms and the electrophysiological signatures associated with these dynamics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Stroop effect is not simply a function of attention but is rather a result of the interaction between attention, perception and response selection.
feature selection is a function of the task characteristics and that the temporal modulation is a function of feature selection.
the Stroop phenomenon is a function of the interplay between early selection processes and later controlled processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
early attentional selection in the Stroops matching task is modulated by both the feature selection mechanism and temporal modulation.
the Stroop effect is a function of the temporal modulation of feature-based processing, and the N1 component reflects this modulation.
the Stroop task is a useful tool for the examination of early feature selection and temporal dynamics in the human brain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Stroop effect is not a function of the time of stimulus onset, but rather the time of the stimulus offset.
early selection processing plays a significant role in Stroop matching tasks and that the role of early selection processing is modulated by task characteristics such as stimulus onset asynchrony.
the Stroop effect can be explained by a combination of early and late attentional mechanisms.
